title: Payment Gateway Timeout Cascade — Visa Debit Processing Outage

content.summary: A connection pool exhaustion on the Visa debit processing adapter caused a cascade of timeouts across the payment gateway, resulting in 12,400 failed card-present transactions between 14:03 and 14:50 UTC on 2024-01-15.

timeline.event: Alerting fires: payment-gateway p99 latency > 8 s (threshold 3 s)
On-call engineer pages; visa-processor connection pool at 100 % utilisation
Incident declared P1; war-room opened in #incident-p1 Slack channel
Root cause identified: database certificate rotation had not propagated to visa-processor pod secrets
Secret updated; rolling restart of visa-processor initiated
All pods healthy; transaction success rate restored to 99.97 %

content.root_cause: The automated certificate rotation job (cert-rotator v2.3.1) updated the PostgreSQL TLS certificate in Vault but the Kubernetes ExternalSecret operator failed to sync the new version to the visa-processor namespace due to a misconfigured sync interval (value was 0 instead of 300 s). As visa-processor pods attempted to reconnect with the expired certificate, connections were rejected, exhausting the pool and triggering cascading timeouts in the upstream payment-gateway.
contributing_factors: cert-rotator did not emit a structured log on sync failure — only a warning-level unstructured message that was not captured by the alerting pipeline
No canary health check existed for database connectivity independent of live traffic
Connection pool size (50 connections) was not auto-scaled under load

immediate: Manually sync ExternalSecret in visa-processor namespace
Rolling restart of all visa-processor pods
short_term: Fix ExternalSecret syncInterval from 0 to 300 s (PR #4412)
Add cert-rotator structured logging for sync failures (JIRA PAY-8821)
long_term: Implement synthetic canary transactions for database connectivity (JIRA PAY-8830)
Add connection pool autoscaling policy (JIRA PAY-8831)
Integrate cert-rotation status into payment gateway readiness probe
